note: YHWH is spelled out here as "JEHOVAH", a hybrid of the consonants YHWH with the vowels of Adonai; elsewhere the KJV writes LORD. The name was most likely pronounced Yahweh. Context: known in the character the name expresses (medium confidence). Genesis uses the name Yahweh, even in God's speech to the patriarchs (15:7; 28:13). In 6:6-7 'you shall know that I am Yahweh' means experiencing the name through redemption, so the contrast is one of revelation, not vocabulary. The rendering keeps the Hebrew open; the KJV difference is only the form of the name. Other possible meanings: (1) the name itself was unknown before Moses, and Genesis uses it anachronistically — many source-critical scholars (assigning 6:3 to P); (2) a rhetorical question, 'by my name Yahweh did I not make myself known to them?' — a minority of interpreters; (3) the patriarchs received the promises but not their fulfilment, which the name signifies — Rashi.
